reasoning_traces.think:
The primitives define a structured approach to causal discovery using conditional independence tests and orientation rules. The first primitive constructs the PAG skeleton by removing edges between conditionally independent nodes, forming the base structure. The second encodes the hierarchical execution of orientation rules, ensuring logical consistency in causal inference. The third applies discriminative path analysis to orient edges based on separation sets. These operations collectively enable the identification of invariant causal structures from observational data. Failure modes include incorrect application of rules when dependencies are mischaracterized or when latent variables introduce ambiguity. Dualities arise in how paths and separators interact to determine edge directions. The system exhibits robustness under known conditional independence assumptions but may fail under model misspecification or unobserved confounding.
